A region is bounded by the curve $y=-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$, as shown above. Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}-\operatorname{csc}⁡\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =1-2 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is 

$$
A=-{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x=1.
$$
